At 61°W, the coast of Ellesmere is further south, around 82.5°N (Alert is 82.5°N, 62.3°W). So 83.0°N, 61°W is about 50 km north of Alert, in the Arctic Ocean, which is sea ice-covered water.

Water

600.text:

Greenland's northern coast at about 83.6°N near Cape Morris Jesup (~33°W). At 59°W, Greenland's north coast is about 82.0-82.5°N (Hall Land/Nyeboe Land area, around 82.2°N). Water

609.text:

972.text:
Latitude 79.0°N, longitude 35.0°W is in northeast Greenland. Greenland's northeast coast near 79°N, where Nioghalvfjerdsfjorden sits, is around 20°W, and the coast at 79°N extends to about 18°W. At 35°W the location is inland, on the ice sheet. Greenland's land spans roughly 20°W to 60°W at that latitude. At 35°W, 79°N, the point is within the ice sheet, which counts as land.

Land

973.text:
Latitude 79.0, longitude -33.0 is in northeast Greenland, inland of the coast. Greenland's northeast coast near 79°N is around -18° to -20° (Norske Øer), and the land extends west to about -60°. At -33°, 79°N is on the Greenland ice sheet, so it's land.

Land

974.text:
Latitude 79.0°N, longitude 31.0°W is in northeastern Greenland. Northeast Greenland National Park extends to about 12°W at this latitude, and the coast around 79°N lies roughly between 18°W and 20°W. Places such as Nioghalvfjerdsfjorden (79°N, about 20°W) are further east than this point, so 31°W is inland, on the ice sheet.

Land

975.text:
Latitude 79°N, longitude 29°W is in northeast Greenland. Greenland's northeast coast near 79°N, around Nioghalvfjerdsfjorden (the 79 Glacier), sits at roughly 20°W. At 29°W and 79°N, that is inland, on the ice sheet or in Dronning Louise Land and Kronprins Christian Land. The coast at this latitude is around 18-20°W, and the land extends west to about 60°W. So 29°W is inland.

Land

976.text:
Latitude 79°N, longitude 27°W is in northeast Greenland. Greenland's northeast coast near 79°N runs around 18–20°W at Norske Øer, and the coast at 79°N is roughly at 18°W. Going west to 27°W at 79°N is within the Greenland interior (Greenland ice sheet / Dronning Louise Land / Kronprins Christian Land), so it is land.

Checking the details: Nioghalvfjerdsfjorden sits at about 79.5°N, 22°W. The inland area at 27°W is the ice sheet, so land.

Land

977.text:
Latitude 79.0°N, longitude 25.0°W is in northeastern Greenland. Greenland's northeast coast near 79°N runs from about 18–20°W at Norske Øer, and the land extends west of that. At 25°W, 79°N, this is inland on the Greenland ice sheet, in Dronning Louise Land / Kronprins Christian Land area. Inland ice at roughly 25°W is land.

Land

978.text:
Latitude 79.0°N, longitude 23.0°W lies in northeastern Greenland. Northeast Greenland National Park covers that area. Greenland's northeast coast runs around 80°N at about 15-20°W, and the Greenland Sea lies east of it. At 79°N the coast is near 18-20°W, with Norske Øer and Belgica Bank offshore. Belgica Bank is at about 78.5°N, 15°W. Westward at 23°W, the point is inland of the coast, roughly at Dronning Louise Land and Kronprins Christian Land. Kronprins Christian Land sits at about 80°N, 20°W. Dronning Louise Land is around 77, -23. Around 79°N, 23°W is near Nioghalvfjerdsfjorden, whose glacier is at 79.5°N, 22°W. The fjord's floating glacier tongue extends to about 20°W. At 23°W, 79°N it is probably ice sheet, so land.

Land

979.text:
Latitude 79.0°N, longitude 21.0°W is in northeast Greenland. Northeast Greenland National Park extends to about 12°W at that latitude, and the coast near 79°N lies around 18–20°W. Around 79°N the Greenland coast is at roughly 18°W, because Nioghalvfjerdsfjorden (the 79 North Glacier) is at about 22°W, 79.5°N. Its floating ice tongue extends to about 20°W. At 79.0°N, 21°W the land is likely inland, since the fjord lies to the north at about 79.5°N. Dove Bugt is further east, and Store Koldewey is around 76°N. So 79°N, 21°W is probably the ice-sheet margin, which counts as land.

Land

980.text:
Latitude 79.0°N, longitude 19.0°W is in northeast Greenland. Greenland's northeast coast near 79°N runs around 18–20°W at Nioghalvfjerdsfjorden (the 79 North Glacier), where the coast is roughly 20°W. Several points have to be checked.

Nioghalvfjerdsfjorden's glacier is at about 79.5°N, 22°W. Further east, Norske Øer is at about 79°N, 19°W. The islands there include Lambert Land at 79.5°N and 20°W, and Store Koldewey at 76.5°N. The coastline near 79°N is around 18–20°W, with the Norske Øer ice barrier near 79.4°N, 18–20°W. The point 79, -19 is most likely near Île de France or the coastal waters just off the shore of Norske Øer. Île de France lies at about 78.8°N, 19°W, which is close to our point.

Île de France is at about 78.5–79°N, 18.5–19.5°W, so the point probably falls on it.

**Land**

981.text:
Latitude 79°N, longitude 17°W is in the Greenland Sea or northeast Greenland. Northeast Greenland's coast near 79°N: Nioghalvfjerdsfjorden glacier is around 79.5°N, 22°W. Coast at 79°N is around 18-20°W (Norske Øer around 11°W at 79°N). Greenland's coastline at 79°N extends east to about 11°W (Norske Øer islands, Lambert Land at 20°W). Belgica Bank is at ~79-80°N, 15-17°W, covered in sea ice, ocean. Land near Hovgaard Island (~76.5°N). At 79°N, the Norske Øer are at ~18-20°W, with Store Koldewey further south at 76°N. Ile de France at 76.5°N. Wait, Norske Øer is at 79.3°N, 19°W. Coast further east: Nordostrundingen at 81.4°N, 11.8°W. Belgica Bank is shallow ocean east of 17°W... Position 79,-17 is east of Norske Øer, so water (Belgica Bank, sea ice-covered).

**Water**

982.text:
Latitude 79°N, longitude 15°W is in the Greenland Sea or off northeast Greenland. Northeast Greenland's coast near 79°N lies around 18-20°W at Nioghalvfjerdsfjorden, with the coast extending further east to about 11°W at Norske Øer (around 79.5°N, 18°W). Since Greenland's east coast at 79°N is roughly 10-20°W, the question is whether 15°W falls on land.

Known points: Westward of Norske Øer, the 79 Glacier (Nioghalvfjerdsfjorden) is at 79.5°N, 22°W. Norske Øer islands are at about 20°W. Belgica Bank is at about 78°N, 15°W, which is sea ice-covered ocean. Further east, Ob Bank and Westwind ridges lie in the sea. Coast at 79°N is about 18°W, so 15°W is water.

**Water**

983.text:
Latitude 79.0°N, longitude 13.0°W is in northeast Greenland. Greenland's northeast coast near 79°N lies around 18–20°W at the coast, and Nioghalvfjerdsfjorden glacier is at about 79.5°N, 22°W. The coast at 80°N reaches roughly 12°W near Norske Øer (about 79°N, 18°W), and the Greenland Sea lies east of that. At 13°W, 79°N, this is east of the coastal islands, so it is the Greenland Sea. Belgica Bank is near 79–80°N, 14–17°W, which is ice-covered sea. The Norske Øer islands sit at about 79.0°N, 18–20°W. So 13°W is farther east, in open water.

Water

984.text:
Latitude 79°N, longitude 11°W is in the Greenland Sea, off the northeast coast of Greenland. Northeast Greenland's coast near 79°N lies roughly at 18-20°W at the outer edge, around Norske Øer at about 20°W. At 11°W the point is east of the coast, so it is in the sea (Fram Strait region). Land would only be Svalbard, which is at 10-30°E, so that does not apply.

Water

985.text:
Latitude 79°N, longitude 9°W lies in the Greenland Sea, off the northeast Greenland coast. Northeast Greenland's coast near 79°N, around Nioghalvfjerdsfjorden, is at about 20°W. At 9°W, it is well offshore, in the Greenland Sea. Sea ice is common there, but it is still water.

Water

986.text:
Latitude 79.0°N, longitude 7.0°W lies in the Greenland Sea, off the northeast coast of Greenland. The Greenland coast at that latitude is around 18-20°W, and Svalbard is at about 10-25°E. So 7°W is east of Greenland and west of Svalbard, which puts it in open sea, though it may be covered with sea ice.

Water

987.text:
Latitude 79°N, longitude 5°W is in the Greenland Sea, east of Greenland's northeast coast. Greenland's coast at 79°N is around 18-20°W, with Norwegian Svalbard further east at 10°E or more. So 5°W is open sea, though it may be covered by ice.

Water

988.text:
Latitude 79°N, longitude 3°W lies in the Greenland Sea, northeast of Greenland. Greenland's northeast coast is around 18-20°W at that latitude, and Svalbard is at 10-20°E. So 3°W at 79°N is open sea (the Greenland Sea, Fram Strait).

Water

989.text:
Latitude 79.0°N, longitude 1°W is in the Greenland Sea, north of Greenland's east coast. Greenland's northeast coast near 79°N lies at about 18–20°W. Svalbard is at 10–25°E. So 1°W at 79°N is open sea, between Greenland and Svalbard, in Fram Strait.

Water

990.text:
Latitude 79°N, longitude 1°E lies in the Arctic Ocean/Greenland Sea area, west of Svalbard (which spans about 10°E to 30°E). At 79°N, 1°E, it is north of the Greenland Sea, between Greenland and Svalbard, so it is water.

Water

991.text:
Latitude 79°N, longitude 3°E is in the Arctic Ocean, north of Svalbard's west coast area. Svalbard's westernmost point, Prins Karls Forland, is at about 11°E, and at 79°N the Fram Strait lies between Greenland and Svalbard. So 3°E is water.

Water

992.text:
Latitude 79°N, longitude 5°E is in the Arctic Ocean, north of Svalbard's western coast, in the Fram Strait area. Svalbard's Spitsbergen lies at about 10-20°E at 79°N. The west coast of Spitsbergen is around 10-11°E at that latitude, so 5°E is in the sea.

Water

993.text:
Latitude 79.0°N, longitude 7.0°E is in the Fram Strait / Greenland Sea, west of Svalbard. Svalbard's western coast (Prins Karls Forland, Spitsbergen) lies around 10–11°E at 79°N. Krossfjorden is around 12°E, so at 7°E the point is west of the coast, in open sea.

Water

994.text:
Latitude 79°N, longitude 9°E is northwest of Svalbard. Spitsbergen's northwest coast reaches about 79.5°N at around 10-11°E, and Krossfjorden sits near 79.2°N, 11.5°E. At 9°E and 79°N, we're west of Spitsbergen's west coast, which lies around 11°E at that latitude (Kongsfjorden at 78.9°N, 12°E). The coast near Prins Karls Forland is at about 78.5°N, 10.5°E. So 9°E, 79°N is in the Greenland Sea/Fram Strait.

Water

995.text:
Latitude 79.0°N, longitude 11.0°E is in the Svalbard area. Spitsbergen's west coast lies around 11-12°E at 79°N. Kongsfjorden is at about 78.95°N, 12°E. Krossfjorden is at about 79.2°N, 11.5°E. At 79°N, 11°E, the point is west of the Brøggerhalvøya peninsula, which extends to roughly 11.1°E at 78.9°N. Brøggerhalvøya's west tip is near Kapp Mitra, around 11.0°E, 78.95°N. At 79.0°N, 11.0°E, that is likely in the sea north of the peninsula, since Kongsfjorden's mouth lies between 78.95 and 79.05°N and the outer coast there is around 11.0°E. Mouth of Kongsfjorden: Prins Heinrich Island sits at about 79.1°N, 11.2°E. The coast of Brøggerhalvøya at 79.0° is near 11.3°E. So the point is likely water.

Water

996.text:
Latitude 79.0°N, longitude 13.0°E is in the Svalbard region. Spitsbergen's west coast lies around 11-12°E at 79°N. Krossfjorden and Kongsfjorden are near 79°N, 12°E. Ny-Ålesund is at 78.92°N, 11.93°E. At 79.0°N, 13°E, we are east of Kongsfjorden, inland between Kongsfjorden and Krossfjorden... Krossfjorden's head is around 79.2°N, 12.5°E. Lilliehöökfjorden is at 79.3°N, 12.3°E. At 79.0°N, 13°E, it is likely land (the Brøggerhalvøya is further west; the inland to the east holds glaciers such as Kongsvegen). Monacobreen is at 79.4°N, 12.5°E. So at 79.0°N, 13°E it is the land area, likely glacier.

Land

997.text:
Latitude 79.0°N, longitude 15.0°E is in the Svalbard region. Spitsbergen spans roughly 10°E to 27°E and 76.5°N to 80.8°N. At 79°N, the west coast of Spitsbergen sits around 11°E, with Krossfjorden and Kongsfjorden near 12°E. Kongsfjorden is at about 78.9°N, 12°E. At 15°E and 79°N, that is inland, near Woodfjorden's area. Woodfjorden's head is at about 79.5°N, 14°E. Raudfjorden lies around 79.8°N, 12.5°E. So 79°N, 15°E is probably land, in Haakon VII Land or New Friesland, east of Krossfjorden. Magdalenefjorden is at 79.6°N, 11°E. The area at 79°N, 15°E is mountainous interior, so land.

Land

998.text:
Latitude 79.0°N, longitude 17.0°E lies in the Svalbard region. Spitsbergen's west coast is around 11-14°E at 79°N. At 79°N, Spitsbergen's northwest corner is near 10-12°E, and Krossfjorden and Kongsfjorden are at about 12°E. At 17°E and 79°N, we're on the north coast of Spitsbergen, near Woodfjorden (about 13-14°E) and Wijdefjorden (about 16-17°E). Wijdefjorden runs from about 79.5°N down to 78.4°N, at roughly 16°E. The fjord is long and narrow, and 17°E at 79°N might be land on its eastern side. Eastern side of Wijdefjorden is Ny-Friesland, which extends to about 18-19°E. The fjord's center is about 16.3°E at 79°N, so 17.0 is probably land.

Land

999.text:
Latitude 79°N, longitude 19°E is in the Svalbard region. Spitsbergen spans roughly 77–80°N and 10–27°E. At 79°N, the west coast of Spitsbergen sits around 11°E, and the northern coast near 80°N. Hence 19°E at 79°N would be inland, probably in Ny-Friesland or near Wijdefjorden. Wijdefjorden lies at about 16°E, running from 79.5°N down to 78.5°N. At 19°E, 79°N, that is east of the fjord, in Ny-Friesland, which is land. Lomfjorden is around 17.5°E and 78.5°N. Ny-Friesland covers 17–19°E, and the east coast sits around 18–20°E at 79°N: Hinlopen Strait is at about 19-20°E for latitude 79.5°N. At 79°N, the Hinlopen coast is around 18.5°E (Duvefjorden is farther north). I think the coast at 79°N is around 18°E... Hinlopen Strait runs from 79.5°N, 19°E at Lomfjorden mouth (Lomfjorden's mouth is at ~79.0°N, 17.5°E?). Actually, Lomfjorden's mouth is at about 78.5°N, 18.5°E, and Hinlopen at 79°N is about 19.5°E. Therefore 19°E is likely land.

Land

1000.text:
Latitude 79°N, longitude 21°E is in the Svalbard area. Nordaustlandet spans roughly 79-80.5°N, 18-27°E. At 79.0°N, 21°E, that is near the southern coast of Nordaustlandet, which is around 79.5°N at 21°E... Let's think about it. Spitsbergen's east coast is around 18-19°E at 79°N, bordering Hinlopen Strait, which lies at about 79.5-80.5°N, 18-20°E. South of that, Wahlenbergfjorden and Murchisonfjorden lie further north. At 79°N, 21°E, we are east of Spitsbergen, in the Storfjorden/Freemansundet area. Barentsøya is around 78.4°N, 21°E, and Edgeøya is at 77.8°N. Nordaustlandet's southern tip is around Kapp Mohn at about 79.5°N, 21-22°E, and the Duvefjorden coast is at about 79.6°N. So 79.0°N, 21°E is likely in the sea north of Barentsøya, which makes it Water.

**Water**

1001.text:
Latitude 79°N, longitude 23°E is in the Svalbard archipelago. Nordaustlandet spans roughly 14°E to 27°E at latitudes of about 79.5° to 80.5°. At 79.0°N, 23°E, it lies south of Nordaustlandet and east of Spitsbergen. Spitsbergen's east coast is around 18-19°E at that latitude, and Edgeøya is at about 78°N, 22°E, so 79°N, 23°E falls in Storfjorden or Freemansundet, north of Edgeøya. Barentsøya spans roughly 78.3-78.6°N, so 79°N is north of it. The southern coast of Nordaustlandet is at about 79.5°N. So 79.0°N, 23°E is in the strait of Hinlopen's southern outlet, which is open sea.

Water

1002.text:
Latitude 79°N, longitude 25°E is in the Svalbard region. Nordaustlandet spans roughly 79-80.5°N and 18-28°E. At 79.0°N, 25°E, that is near the southern coast of Nordaustlandet. Its southern coast lies around 79.5°N at longitude 20-22°E, and Wahlenbergfjorden is at about 79.3°N, 20°E. Further east, Duvefjorden and Rijpfjorden are on the north side. The southeast of Nordaustlandet, near Zorgdragerfjellet, is around 79.4°N, 22°E. Kapp Heuglin is at about 79.0°N, 24°E? Actually, Storfjorden separates Spitsbergen from Edgeøya, and Nordaustlandet's south coast faces Hinlopen Strait only on the west side. Its southern coast on the east side is at about 79.5°N, 25°E (Kapp Leigh Smith, Bråsvellbreen, an ice cap outlet around 79.8°N, 24°E). So 79.0°N, 25°E is south of that coast in open sea (Barents Sea), north of Kong Karls Land (at 79°N, 26-28°E). Kong Karls Land islands: Kongsøya is at 78.9°N, 28.5°E; Svenskøya at 78.7°N, 28°E. So 25°E is west of them, so water.

Water

1003.text:
Latitude 79.0°N, longitude 27.0°E is in the Svalbard region. Nordaustlandet spans roughly 79-80.5°N and 18-28°E. At 27°E, 79°N, the northeastern part of Nordaustlandet's coast... The island's southern coast is around 79.5°N at 22-27°E (Duvefjorden, Wahlenbergfjorden at ~79.5N, 20E). The east coast, near Kapp Mohn... Zorgdragerfjellet is at 79.9N, 22E. The southeast of Nordaustlandet includes Torell Land (south of 79°?), Kong Ludwig Land. Actually, Storøya is at 80.2N, 29E. Kvitøya further east. The Nordaustlandet southeastern coast along Palanderbukta (79.6N, 22E)... Zeipelodden at 79.0N? Zeipelodden is on Barentsøya? Actually Kapp Heuglin is on Edgeøya (~77.5N). Nordaustlandet's southern tip is Kapp Mohn (~79.3N, 24E?) and Kræmerpynten (~79.2N, 24.5E)? The coast east of that runs northeast to Kapp Leighton... Overall at 79.0N, 27E, the point lies south of the coast, in Storfjorden/Barents Sea. Water.

**Water**

1004.text:
Latitude 79°N, longitude 29°E is in the Svalbard region. Nordaustlandet spans roughly 14°E to 28°E, and Kvitøya sits at about 80.2°N, 32.5°E. At 79°N, 29°E, the nearest land would be the eastern edge of Nordaustlandet, whose east coast is around 27–28°E at latitude 79.7°N, but lower down, near 79°N, there is no land there. Edgeøya lies at 77.5°N, so it is too far south. That leaves open sea, the Barents Sea.

Water

1005.text:
Latitude 79.0°N, longitude 31.0°E lies in the Svalbard archipelago region. Nordaustlandet spans roughly 79–80.5°N and 18–28°E. Kvitøya is at about 80.1°N, 32.5°E. Kong Karls Land is at about 78.9°N, 28–29°E. So 79°N, 31°E lies east of Kong Karls Land and south of Kvitøya, which is open sea in the Barents Sea.

Water

1006.text:
Latitude 79.0°N, longitude 33.0°E lies in the Svalbard region. Nordaustlandet spans roughly 79–80.5°N and 18–28°E. East of that, at 33°E and 79°N, is the Barents Sea. Kvitøya sits at about 80.2°N, 32.5°E, which is further north. Kong Karls Land is at about 78.9°N, 28°E. So 33°E at 79°N is open water.

Water

1007.text:
Latitude 79.0°N, longitude 35.0°E is in the Arctic, in the Svalbard region. Nordaustlandet spans roughly 18°E to 28°E, and Kvitøya sits at about 80.2°N, 32.5°E. Kong Karls Land is at about 78.9°N, 26-29°E. So 35°E at 79°N is east of all of these, which puts it in the Barents Sea.

**Water**

1008.text:
Latitude 79.0°N, longitude 37.0°E lies in the Arctic, in the Svalbard region. Nordaustlandet spans roughly 18°E to 28°E, and Kvitøya is at about 80°N, 32.5°E. Franz Josef Land begins around 44°E, with its western islands near 45–50°E. At 37°E and 79°N there are no islands, so this is the Barents Sea.

Water

1009.text:
Latitude 79°N, longitude 39°E lies in the Svalbard/Franz Josef Land region. Nordaustlandet in Svalbard spans roughly 18°E to 28°E, so 39°E is east of it. Franz Josef Land starts at about 45°E. Kvitøya sits at about 80°N, 32.5°E. At 79°N, 39°E, that falls in the Barents Sea, between Svalbard and Franz Josef Land.

Water

1010.text:
Latitude 79.0°N, longitude 41.0°E lies in the Arctic, in the Svalbard/Franz Josef Land region. Franz Josef Land spans about 80–81.8°N and 44–65°E. Kvitøya (Svalbard) is at about 80.1°N, 32.5°E. Nordaustlandet extends to about 27°E. So 79°N, 41°E is in the Barents Sea, east of Svalbard and south of Franz Josef Land, and there is no land there.

Water

1011.text:
Latitude 79.0°N, longitude 43.0°E. This lies in the Arctic, near Franz Josef Land (about 80°N, 45–65°E) and Svalbard's Nordaustlandet (about 80°N, 15–28°E). Franz Josef Land's westernmost islands, such as Cape Tegetthoff on Hall Island and Bell Island, sit around 46–50°E. The point at 43°E and 79°N is west of these islands, in the Barents Sea. Novaya Zemlya's northern tip is around 77°N, 69°E, so it is not close. Kvitøya is at 80°N, 32°E, which is also not close.

Water

1012.text:
Latitude 79.0°N, longitude 45.0°E. That lands in the Arctic, in Franz Josef Land, which spans roughly 80–81.8°N and 44–66°E. At 79°N, 45°E, it is just south of the archipelago's southern edge. The southernmost islands, such as Hall Island, Hooker Island, and Northbrook Island, lie around 80°N, so this point is probably in the Barents Sea. Novaya Zemlya's northern tip is near 77°N, 68°E, which is farther east, so it doesn't apply. Svalbard's Nordaustlandet reaches only about 28°E, so it doesn't apply either. The point is therefore in open water.

Water

1013.text:
Latitude 79.0°N, longitude 47.0°E lies in the Arctic, in the Franz Josef Land archipelago, which spans roughly 42°E to 63°E and 80°N to 81.8°N. At 79°N it sits south of that archipelago. Novaya Zemlya's northern tip is around 77°N, 68°E, so it is further east. Svalbard's Nordaustlandet reaches about 27°E at most. Kvitøya is at 80°N, 32°E. So 79°N, 47°E falls in the Barents Sea, between Svalbard and Franz Josef Land, which is water.

Water

1014.text:
Latitude 79°N, longitude 49°E is in the Franz Josef Land region, which spans roughly 42°E–65°E and 80°N–81.8°N, with its southernmost islands around 79.8°N. At 79.0°N, 49°E, that is south of the archipelago, in the Barents Sea. Novaya Zemlya's northern tip reaches about 77°N at around 68°E, so it is not near this point. Kvitøya is at 80°N, 32°E, which is also far away. Franz Josef Land's southwestern islands, such as Bell Island (Ostrov Bell), are near 80.0°N, 50°E. So 79°N is south of them, which makes this water.

Water

1015.text:
Latitude 79.0°N, longitude 51.0°E. That lies in the Franz Josef Land archipelago, which spans roughly 80-82°N and 45-65°E, with its southern islands at about 80°N. At 79°N, 51°E, it is likely just south of the archipelago, in the Barents Sea. The southernmost island, Cape Kohlsaat on Hooker Island... actually, the southern islands (Alexandra Land, Hayes, etc.) are around 80.0-80.8°N. Nothing is at 79°N there, though Kvitøya (80°N, 32°E) is far west and Victoria Island is at 80°N, 36°E. So this point is water.

Water

1016.text:
Latitude 79.0°N, longitude 53.0°E. That is in the Arctic, in the Franz Josef Land archipelago, which spans roughly 79–81.8°N and 44–65°E. Franz Josef Land's southern islands include Hooker Island (~80.3°N, 52.8°E), Northbrook Island (~79.9°N, 50°E), and Hall Island (~80.2°N, 58°E). Alexandra Land lies at ~80.9°N. The southernmost point of the archipelago is around 79.7°N (Cape Grant, Bell Island at ~80.0°N, 50°E). So 79.0°N is south of all of the islands and falls in the Barents Sea.

Novaya Zemlya's northern tip is at about 77°N, 68°E, which is farther east, so 53°E at 79°N isn't land there either.

Water

1017.text:
Latitude 79°N, longitude 55°E: this is in the Franz Josef Land region (which spans roughly 80-82°N, 45-65°E) or just south of it. Franz Josef Land's southernmost islands are at around 80°N (Cape Kohlsaat, Hooker Island at 80.3°N). Novaya Zemlya's northern tip is around 77°N, 69°E. At 79°N, 55°E, that lies in the Barents Sea, south of Franz Josef Land. The southernmost island, Alexandra Land, is at about 80.7°N. Further southwest, Kvitøya is at 80°N, 32°E. So 79°N, 55°E is water.

Water

1311.text:
Latitude 75.0 N, longitude -77.0 W falls in the Canadian Arctic, near northern Baffin Island and Devon Island. Lancaster Sound lies at about 74°N, 84°W to 80°W, and Baffin Island's northern tip is around 73.7°N, 80°W. At 77°W, the northwest Greenland coast is at about 77°W, 76-78°N, which is farther north.

Near 75°N, 77°W we are in northern Baffin Bay, west of Greenland (Greenland's west coast is around 58-70°W at that latitude). Devon Island's southeast coast runs near 74.5°N, 80°W, and its eastern end is around 75°N, 79°W (Cape Sherard is at 74.6°N, 80.4°W). Bylot Island sits at about 73.2°N, 78°W. So 75°N, 77°W lies east of Devon Island and north of Bylot, in Baffin Bay, which is water.

**Water**

1312.text:
Latitude 75°N, longitude 75°W is in northwest Greenland, near Thule/Qaanaaq, though Baffin Bay lies slightly to the west. Thule Air Base is at about 76.5°N, 68.7°W. At 75°N, 75°W, the coast of Greenland near Melville Bay is at roughly 75.5°N, 59°W, which is much farther east. Baffin Island's northern coast is around 73°N, 80°W. Ellesmere Island's southern part (Devon Island, at 75.0°N, 80°W) is at the edge as well. At 75°N, 75°W the spot lies in Lancaster Sound/northern Baffin Bay. Lancaster Sound sits at about 74°N, 80–85°W, and Devon Island's east tip is around 74.5°N, 80°W. The point at 75°N, 75°W is east of that, in open northern Baffin Bay, so it is water.

Water

1313.text:
Latitude 75.0°N, longitude 73.0°W lies in northwest Greenland, near Thule/Qaanaaq. Pituffik (Thule Air Base) is at about 76.5°N, 68.7°W. Qaanaaq is at 77.5°N, 69°W. At 75°N, 73°W, this is in Baffin Bay or on the coast? Greenland's west coast at 75°N is around 58-60°W, because the coast near Upernavik (72.8°N, 56°W) and Melville Bay (75.5°N, ~60°W). So 73°W at 75°N is well west of the coast, which puts it in Baffin Bay. Baffin Island's northeast coast is around 72°N, 75°W (Pond Inlet is 72.7°N, 77.9°W), and Bylot Island is at 73°N, 78°W. So 75°N, 73°W is in the water of northern Baffin Bay.

Water

1314.text:
Latitude 75°N, longitude 71°W is in northwestern Greenland, near Thule/Pituffik. Pituffik is at 76.5°N, 68.7°W. At 75°N, 71°W, that is south of Pituffik, near Melville Bay. The Greenland coast around 75.5°N is at about 59-60°W in the Melville Bay region, and in the Thule area the coast is around 77°N. Baffin Bay lies west of Greenland. At 75°N, the Greenland coast is around 58–60°W, so 71°W is well into Baffin Bay. Baffin Island's northern coast at 71°W is around 70°N, and Bylot Island is at 73°N, 78°W. So 75°N, 71°W is in the water of northern Baffin Bay.

Water

1315.text:
The point 75.0°N, 69.0°W is in northwest Greenland, near Thule/Pituffik, which is at about 76.5°N, 68.8°W. At 75°N, 69°W, I think this is in Melville Bay. Melville Bay's coast runs around 75-76°N at 60-62°W, and Greenland's coast at 69°W lies near 76.4°N (Pituffik). So at 75°N, 69°W we are south of Thule, inland on the ice sheet. The Greenland coast near Cape York (75.9°N, 66.4°W) runs southeast. At 69°W the coast lies at about 76.3°N, so 75°N is well inland, on the ice sheet.

Land

1316.text:
Latitude 75.0°N, longitude 67.0°W is in northwest Greenland, near Thule/Pituffik. Pituffik is at 76.5°N, 68.7°W. At 75°N, 67°W, that's south of Pituffik, near the Melville Bay area. The Greenland coast at 75°N is around 58–60°W, and the ice sheet lies east of that. 67°W at 75°N lies west of the coast, so it falls in Baffin Bay, which is water.

Checking further: Baffin Bay at 75°N spans from Greenland (~60°W) to Devon Island/Baffin Island (~80°W). 67°W is therefore in the bay.

**Water**

1317.text:
Latitude 75°N, longitude 65°W: this is in northwest Greenland / Baffin Bay area. Thule (Pituffik) is at 76.5N, 68.7W. At 75N, 65W... Greenland's coast near there: Melville Bay's coast is around 75.5N, 59W to 61W at the ice edge. Greenland's west coast at 75N is around 58-60W. So 65W at 75N is in Baffin Bay, which is to the west of the coast. Baffin Bay spans to Baffin Island's coast at ~72N, 70W. At 75N, Devon Island's southeast coast is around 80W. So 65W is water.

**Water**

1318.text:
Latitude 75.0°N, longitude 63.0°W is in northwest Greenland, near Baffin Bay. Thule (Pituffik) sits at about 76.5°N, 68.7°W. At 75°N, the Greenland coast lies around 58–60°W, and 63°W is at roughly the same latitude as Melville Bay's coast. Melville Bay's coastline at 75°N is about 59–60°W. The area west of that is Baffin Bay, which is water. Ellesmere Island is farther north and west, at about 76°N and 80°W. So 63°W is in Baffin Bay.

Water

1319.text:
Latitude 75.0°N, longitude 61.0°W is in northwest Greenland, near Melville Bay. Thule (Pituffik) is at about 76.5°N, 68.7°W. At 75°N, the Greenland coast around Melville Bay runs from about 59°W to 74°W, so the question is whether 61°W is on land or in the bay. Upernavik is at 72.8°N, 56°W. The Melville Bay coast near 75°N lies at about 58-60°W, with the ice sheet edge around 60°W. Cape York is at about 75.9°N, 66.5°W. Moving south from Cape York, the coast trends southeast, and at 75°N it lies at about 60°W. Where Melville Bay coast meets 75°N is uncertain. Kap Seddon is at 75.2°N, 59°W, and Dronning Louise Land is nearby. So 61°W at 75°N is likely just west of the coast, in the water, though the coast could also be farther west. Islands in the area include the Sabine Islands and Kap Walker. Kap Walker is at about 75.1°N, 61.5°W, which suggests the coast is near 61°W, with the area near there being glacier fronts. Since the ice sheet reaches the coast around there, the point could be on land or ice. I'll say Land.

Land

1320.text:
Latitude 75.0°N, longitude 59.0°W is in northwest Greenland, near Melville Bay. Upernavik is at about 72.8°N, 56°W. At 75°N, the coast of Melville Bay runs from around 61°W at 76°N down to about 56°W at 74°N, so I need to work out where 59°W falls. Cape York is at about 76°N, 68°W. Melville Bay's coast: Kap Seddon about 75.0°N, 59.5°W?

The ice sheet edge in this area is around 74.5–75.5°N and 58–60°W. Savissivik is at 76°N, 65°W. The coast near 75°N is probably around 59–60°W, where Kap Seddon and Kap Walker lie, so the point is likely at or just inland of the coast. Melville Bay's open water lies west of that, around 60–62°W. Greenland's coast at 75°N is roughly 59.5°W, so 59°W is just inland.

**Land**

1321.text:
Latitude 75.0°N, longitude 57.0°W is in northwest Greenland, near Melville Bay. Upernavik is at about 72.8°N, 56°W. Thule (Qaanaaq) is at 77.5°N, 69°W. At 75°N, 57°W, the Greenland coast in Melville Bay runs around 75.5°N at about 59°W, and the ice sheet edge lies further east. The coast near Cape York is at 76°N, 68°W. In Melville Bay, the coastline at 57°W is probably around 74.5–75°N, with islands, and the point itself would be on the ice sheet or the bay.

Looking closer: Melville Bay's coast runs from Kap Seddon (about 74.3°N, 56.5°W) up to Kap Walker (75.9°N, 60°W). At 57°W the coast is about 74.5°N, so 75°N, 57°W would be north of the coast, which is inland. That makes it land (ice sheet).

Land

1322.text:
Latitude 75.0°N, longitude 55.0°W lies in northwest Greenland, near Melville Bay. Upernavik is at about 72.8°N, 56°W. At 75°N, the coast near Melville Bay runs from roughly 75.5°N, 59°W (Cape York is at 76°N, 68°W). Around 75°N, the coast is near 58–60°W, so 55°W is inland, on the ice sheet.

Land

1323.text:
Latitude 75°N, longitude 53°W is in northwest Greenland, near Melville Bay. The Greenland coast at that longitude lies around 76°N, and the ice sheet extends inland. At 75°N, 53°W, the coast sits roughly at 59-60°W, near Upernavik (72.8°N, 56°W). Melville Bay's coast runs from about 75.5°N, 59°W down to 73°N, 56°W. So at 53°W the point is well inland on the ice sheet.

Land

1324.text:
Latitude 75.0°N, longitude 51.0°W is in Greenland, but I should check whether it falls on the ice sheet or in the water. The west coast of Greenland near Upernavik is at about 72.8°N, 56°W. At 75°N, the coast is near Melville Bay, around 59–60°W. At 51°W the point is well inland, on the ice sheet, which counts as land.

Land

1325.text:
Latitude 75°N, longitude 49°W is in Greenland. The northwest coast of Greenland near Melville Bay lies around 75–76°N and 58–65°W. At 49°W, the ice sheet covers the interior, and the east coast sits around 20–25°W at that latitude. So 49°W at 75°N is well inland on the ice sheet.

Land

1326.text:
Latitude 75°N, longitude 47°W is in central Greenland, on the ice sheet. The coast there is farther east, since Greenland's east coast at 75°N is around 18–20°W, and the west coast is around 58–60°W. So 47°W falls inside the island.

Land

1327.text:
Latitude 75°N, longitude 45°W is in central Greenland, which is land.

Land

1328.text:
Latitude 75°N, longitude 43°W is in central Greenland, which is covered by the ice sheet. That makes it land.

Land

1329.text:
Latitude 75°N, longitude 41°W falls in central-eastern Greenland, on the ice sheet. Greenland's east coast at 75°N is around 18-22°W, and the west coast is around 58-70°W. So 41°W is well inland, on the ice sheet.

Land

1330.text:
Latitude 75.0°N, longitude 39.0°W falls in central Greenland. Greenland's east coast around 75°N lies at roughly 18–20°W, and the west coast is near 60°W or further. Longitude 39°W is therefore well inland, on the ice sheet.

Land

1331.text:
Latitude 75°N, longitude 37°W is in central-east Greenland. Greenland's east coast at around 75°N sits near 18-20°W, and the ice sheet extends west from there. At 37°W the point is inland, on the ice sheet, so it is land.

Land

1332.text:
Latitude 75°N, longitude 35°W is in northeastern Greenland. Greenland's northeast coast near 75°N lies around 18–20°W, and the ice sheet extends west of that, so 35°W is inland.

Land

1333.text:
Latitude 75°N, longitude 33°W is in central-east Greenland, inland from the coast. Greenland's east coast at 75°N lies around 18–20°W, and the west coast is near 58°W, so 33°W falls inside the island, on the ice sheet.

Land

1334.text:
Latitude 75°N, longitude 31°W is in northeast Greenland. Greenland's east coast at that latitude is around 18-20°W, and the land extends west from there. Around 75°N the coast is near Shannon Island at about 18°W. At 31°W, 75°N, that is inland, within the Greenland ice sheet and the Queen Louise Land area, which is land.

Land

1335.text:
Latitude 75°N, longitude 29°W is in northeast Greenland. Greenland's east coast around 75°N lies at about 18–22°W (Greenland Sea coast near Kong Oscar Fjord at 72°N, ~25°W). At 75°N, the coast is around 18–20°W (Shannon Island ~75°N, 18°W). Longitude 29°W at 75°N is inland, on the ice sheet or in the interior of Greenland, e.g., Dronning Louise Land is ~76°N, 22°W. So 29°W is inland ice.

Land

1336.text:
Latitude 75°N, longitude 27°W is in northeast Greenland. Greenland's east coast around 75°N, with Kong Oscar Fjord and Scoresby Sund further south. At 75°N, the coast is around 18-20°W (Shannon Island is at about 75°N, 18°W). Longitude 27°W at 75°N lies inland, on the Greenland mainland (Stauning Alps are at 72°N, 25°W; Kong Oscar Fjord at 72°N, 24°W). At 75°N, 27°W is in the area of Dronning Louise Land / Hold with Hope region. This is inland, near the ice sheet margin. Land.

**Land**

1337.text:
Latitude 75°N, longitude 25°W is in northeast Greenland, in the area of Kong Oscar Fjord and Traill Island. Traill Island lies at about 72.5°N, and Ella Island at about 73°N, 25°W. At 75°N, 25°W we are near Kejser Franz Joseph Fjord's northern side, close to Ymer Island and Geographical Society Island. The fjord is at about 73°N. At 75°N, the coast of Greenland is at about 20°W, with Wollaston Foreland at 74.5°N, 19.5°W. So 25°W at 75°N lies inland. Places there: Stauning Alps are at 72°N, 25°W. Further north, Hold with Hope is at about 73.5°N, 21°W. The inland ice sheet margin and the Dronning Louise Land area are at roughly 76.5°N, 24°W. So 75°N, 25°W is land, probably the ice sheet or the Lambert Land region.

Land

1338.text:
Latitude 75.0°N, longitude 23.0°W is in northeastern Greenland. The coast there runs roughly from 70°N at Scoresby Sund up to about 81°N. At 75°N the coastline lies around 18-20°W, near Shannon Island and Kuhn Island, and Wollaston Foreland sits at about 74.5°N, 19.5°W. Further inland at 23°W is Kong Oscar Fjord and Kejser Franz Joseph Fjord, which reaches about 27°W at 73°N.

Around 75°N, the Greenland Sea coast has Hochstetter Foreland at about 75°N, 19°W. Moving west, Kejser Franz Joseph Fjord is at about 73.2°N. Just north of it is Ymer Ø at 73°N, 25°W, and Geographical Society Ø at 72.7°N. At 75°N and 23°W, we are north of the fjord system, in the area of Clavering Ø (74.3°N, 20°W) and Wollaston Foreland. West of those lies the land of Traill Land and Ella Ø, and farther north is Lambert Land. At 75°N, 23°W, this appears to be inland: Hold with Hope and Gael Hamke Bugt are at about 74°N, 20°W. Inland it is land, as Greenland's ice-covered interior extends there.

**Land**

1339.text:
Latitude 75°N, longitude 21°W is in northeast Greenland. Land spans roughly from 12°W to 70°W at that latitude, though the northeast coast near 75°N is complicated. Places nearby: Kong Oscar Fjord is at about 72°N, 24°W. Kejser Franz Joseph Fjord is at about 73°N, 24-27°W. Clavering Island is at about 74.3°N, 20°W. Wollaston Foreland is at about 74.5°N, 19-20°W. Shannon Island is at about 75°N, 18°W. Hochstetter Forland is at about 75.2°N, 19.5°W. Gael Hamke Bugt lies around 74.5°N, 20°W. Further north, Koldewey Island is at about 76.7°N, 18.5°W. Mainland Greenland near 75°N extends to Kuhn Island at about 74.9°N, 20.5°W, and Kuhn Island is a notable feature there. Just west is Bessel Fjord and Dove Bugt, but Dove Bugt is at about 76.5°N. Around 75°N, 21°W, the mainland borders Godthåb Gulf (about 74°N, 21°W), with Hold with Hope peninsula at 73.5°N, 21°W. Hold with Hope extends up to about 73.9°N. North of that is Clavering Island, 74°N to 74.5°N, then Wollaston Foreland. At 75°N, 21°W we are likely in Greenland Sea fjord areas such as Godfred Hansen Bay, or on Kuhn Island/mainland. Kuhn Island spans about 74.8-75.0°N, 20-21°W. I'd say Land.

**Land**

1340.text:
Latitude 75.0°N, longitude 19.0°W lies in eastern Greenland. Greenland's east coast around 75°N is at about 18–22°W (Kong Oscar Fjord and Traill Island are near 72°N, 24°W). At 75°N, the Greenland Sea coast near Hold with Hope/Shannon Island: Shannon Island is at about 75°N, 18.5°W. Wollaston Forland is at about 74.5°N, 19–20°W. Shannon Island sits roughly 75.0–75.3°N, 18–19°W. The point is probably right on Shannon Island's west or east side. Shannon Island spans roughly 17.8°W to 19.5°W and 74.8°N to 75.3°N, so the point likely falls on land.

Land

1341.text:
Latitude 75.0°N, longitude 17.0°W is in northeast Greenland, near the coast. Greenland's northeast coast around 75°N: Kuhn Island is at about 75°N, 20°W. Shannon Island is at 75°N, 18°W. Clavering Island is at 74°N, 20°W. Longitude -17 at 75°N lies east of Shannon Island (which spans about 18.5–17.5°W), so it is probably in the Greenland Sea. Shannon Island's east coast is around 17.9°W at 75°N, and Pendulum Islands are at 74.6°N, 18.8°W. Little Pendulum is about 18.9°W. Bass Rock is at 74.5°N, 19°W... Hold Rock islands too. East of Shannon there is open sea, so 17°W is water.

**Water**

1342.text:
Latitude 75°N, longitude 15°W is in the Greenland Sea, off the coast of northeast Greenland. The coast of NE Greenland at 75°N lies around 18–20°W, with Shannon Island at about 18.5°W and Kuhn Island near 20°W. So 15°W is east of those islands, which puts it in the Greenland Sea, and Jan Mayen is farther south at 71°N. The point is in water.

Water

1343.text:
Latitude 75°N, longitude 13°W lies in the Greenland Sea, off the northeast coast of Greenland. The coast of NE Greenland at 75°N: Greenland's coast there, such as Kuhn Island at around 75°N, 20°W, and Shannon Island at 75°N, 18°W. The edge of land is at roughly 18-20°W, so 13°W is east of the coast, in the sea.

Water

1344.text:
Latitude 75.0°N, longitude 11.0°W lies in the Greenland Sea or on the northeast Greenland coast. Northeast Greenland's coast near 75°N sits around 18-20°W at Shannon Island and Sabine Island (about 74.5°N, 18.5°W). At 11°W, it is well east of the coast, which makes it open sea (the Greenland Sea).

Water

1345.text:
Latitude 75°N, longitude 9°W is in the Greenland Sea, northeast of Greenland. Greenland's east coast at 75°N lies around 18-20°W, or farther west where the coast is indented. Jan Mayen is at 71°N, 8°W. At 75°N, 9°W, the area is open sea, though sea ice may cover it.

Water

1346.text:
The point 75°N, 7°W lies in the Greenland Sea, east of Greenland's coast. Greenland's northeast coast at 75°N extends to about 18-20°W, so 7°W is well offshore. Jan Mayen is at 71°N, so it isn't relevant. Svalbard is at 74-80°N but 10-30°E, so it isn't relevant either.

Water

1347.text:
Latitude 75°N, longitude 5°W lies in the Greenland Sea, northeast of Greenland. Greenland's east coast at 75°N is around 18–20°W, and Svalbard is at about 10–25°E. Jan Mayen is at 71°N, 8°W. So 75°N, 5°W is open water.

Water

1348.text:
Latitude 75°N, longitude 3°W. That is in the Greenland Sea, north of Iceland and Jan Mayen (71°N, 8°W). Greenland's east coast at 75°N lies around 18-20°W, so 3°W is well east of it. Svalbard is at 77-80°N and 10-30°E, so it is not near either. The point is in open water.

Water

1349.text:
Latitude 75°N, longitude 1°W is in the Greenland Sea, north of Iceland and east of Greenland. Jan Mayen is at about 71°N, 8°W, and Svalbard starts around 76.5°N, 10°E. Greenland's east coast at 75°N is around 18-20°W. So 1°W is open ocean.

Water

1350.text:
Latitude 75°N, longitude 1°E is in the Greenland Sea/Norwegian Sea north of Norway, between Svalbard and Greenland. Jan Mayen is at 71°N, 8°W, and Svalbard's southern tip is at about 76.5°N, 16°E. So 75°N, 1°E is open ocean.

Water

1351.text:
Latitude 75.0°N, longitude 3.0°E lies in the Greenland Sea/Norwegian Sea region, north of Norway and southeast of Jan Mayen. Svalbard is at 74-80°N but its longitude is 10-30°E. Bear Island is at 74.4°N, 19°E. So 3°E at 75°N is open ocean.

Water

1352.text:
Latitude 75°N, longitude 5°E is in the Greenland Sea/Norwegian Sea region, northwest of Bear Island (74.5°N, 19°E) and well west of Svalbard. Jan Mayen sits at 71°N, 8°W, so it is not nearby. This point is open ocean.

Water

1353.text:
Latitude 75°N, longitude 7°E is in the Greenland Sea/Norwegian Sea area, north of Norway and west of Svalbard. Bear Island is at 74.4°N, 19°E, so it's far to the east. Jan Mayen is at 71°N, 8°W. So 75°N, 7°E is open water.

Water

1354.text:
Latitude 75°N, longitude 9°E lies in the Arctic Ocean, north of Norway. Svalbard spans roughly 74° to 81°N, but only at longitudes of about 10° to 35°E. Bear Island is at 74.4°N, 19°E. At 75°N, 9°E, the point is in the Greenland Sea or Norwegian Sea, which is water.

Water

1355.text:
Latitude 75°N, longitude 11°E lies in the Arctic, north of Norway. Bear Island is at 74.4°N, 19°E, and Spitsbergen's southern tip is at about 76.5°N, 16°E. The point (75, 11) is in the Barents/Greenland Sea, west of Bear Island, so it is water.

Water

1356.text:
Latitude 75°N, longitude 13°E lies in the Barents Sea/Arctic Ocean, between Svalbard (which starts around 76.4°N) and Bear Island (74.4°N, 19°E). Bear Island is at 19°E, so 13°E at 75°N is open sea.

Water

1357.text:
Latitude 75°N, longitude 15°E is in the Arctic Ocean north of Norway, near the Svalbard archipelago. Svalbard sits at roughly 76.5°N–80°N, and Bear Island is at about 74.4°N, 19°E. So 75°N, 15°E lies in the Barents/Norwegian Sea, south-west of Bear Island.

Water

1358.text:
Latitude 75°N, longitude 17°E lies in the Barents Sea, south of Svalbard (which begins around 76.5°N) and north of Bear Island (74.4°N, 19°E). Bear Island is at 74.5°N, 19°E, so 75°N, 17°E is about 60 km northwest of it, which is open water.

Water

1359.text:
Latitude 75°N, longitude 19°E lies in the Barents Sea, between Norway's mainland and Svalbard. Bear Island is at about 74.4°N, 19°E. Bear Island spans roughly 74.35–74.5°N, so 75.0°N is about 35 nautical miles north of it, which puts the point in open water.

Water

1360.text:
Latitude 75°N, longitude 21°E lies in the Barents Sea, south-east of Svalbard (Bear Island is at 74.4°N, 19°E). Svalbard's southern tip is around 76.5°N, so 75°N, 21°E is south of that and east of Bear Island, which makes it open water.

Water

1361.text:
Latitude 75°N, longitude 23°E lies in the Barents Sea, south of Svalbard (Bear Island is at 74.4°N, 19°E). Svalbard's southern tip is around 76.5°N, so 75°N, 23°E is water.

Water

1362.text:
Latitude 75°N, longitude 25°E lies in the Barents Sea, south of Svalbard, whose southern tip (Sørkapp) is at about 76.5°N. Bear Island is at 74.5°N, 19°E, so it is not at this point. Nothing else is nearby, so the point is open water.

Water

1363.text:
Latitude 75°N, longitude 27°E is in the Barents Sea, south-east of Svalbard (Edgeøya is at about 77.7°N, 22.5°E) and north of Bear Island (74.4°N, 19°E). Svalbard's southernmost point is around 76.4°N, so 75°N is south of it. Norway's mainland ends around 71°N. That leaves open sea.

Water

1364.text:
Latitude 75°N, longitude 29°E lies in the Barents Sea, south-east of Svalbard (Edgeøya is around 78°N, 22°E) and north of Norway's North Cape (71°N). Bear Island is at 74.4°N, 19°E, which is well to the west. So this point is open water.

Water

1365.text:
Latitude 75°N, longitude 31°E lies in the Barents Sea, north of Norway and east of Svalbard's southern tip. Bear Island is at about 74.4°N, 19°E, and Svalbard's Edgeøya is at roughly 77.5°N, 22°E. Kong Karls Land is at about 78.8°N, 28°E. Novaya Zemlya is much farther east, at 70-76°N and 52-68°E. So 75°N, 31°E is open sea.

Water

1366.text:
Latitude 75°N, longitude 33°E lies in the Barents Sea, north of Norway and Russia and south of Svalbard. Svalbard's southern tip is around 76.5°N, and Bear Island is at about 74.5°N, 19°E. Nothing at 75°N, 33°E is land, so this point is water.

Water

1367.text:
Latitude 75°N, longitude 35°E is in the Barents Sea, east of Svalbard and north of Norway and Russia. Svalbard spans roughly 10–35°E at latitudes 76.5–80.5°N, so 75°N is south of it. Bear Island sits at 74.4°N, 19°E, which is far to the west. Novaya Zemlya starts at about 51°E. So this point is open sea.

Water

1368.text:
Latitude 75°N, longitude 37°E lies in the Barents Sea, north of Norway and Russia and south of Svalbard. Novaya Zemlya starts around 51°E, and Svalbard's southern tip is near 76.5°N, so this point is open sea.

Water

1369.text:
Latitude 75°N, longitude 39°E lies in the Barents Sea, north of Novaya Zemlya's southern part and east of Svalbard. Novaya Zemlya spans about 51°E to 69°E, so 39°E is well west of it. Franz Josef Land starts at about 45°E, and Svalbard's Edgeøya reaches about 28°E at 77°N. So 75°N 39°E is open sea.

Water

1370.text:
Latitude 75°N, longitude 41°E lies in the Barents Sea, east of Svalbard and northwest of Novaya Zemlya. Novaya Zemlya's southern island spans roughly 52°E to 69°E, so 41°E is well to its west. Franz Josef Land starts around 45°E but sits at latitude 80°N or higher. So this point is open sea.

Water

1371.text:

Water

1373.text:

Water

1374.text:
Latitude 75°N, longitude 49°E is in the Arctic. Novaya Zemlya spans roughly 51°E to 69°E at latitudes 70°N to 77°N. At 49°E, 75°N, that is west of Novaya Zemlya's southwestern coast, in the Barents Sea. The southern island's western coast at about 75°N lies near 56-57°E. So 49°E is in the sea.

Water

1375.text:

1376.text:

1377.text:
Latitude 75°N, longitude 55°E lies in the Arctic, in the Novaya Zemlya region. Novaya Zemlya runs from about 70.5°N to 77°N, between roughly 51°E and 69°E. At 75°N the archipelago's western coast is around 56–58°E, so 55°E could be just west of the coast, in the Barents Sea. The southern island is wide at 73–74°N, with its west coast near 54–55°E. Farther north, at 75–76°N, the coast bends northeast. Cape Zhelaniya is at 77°N, 69°E. Around 75°N the west coast is near 59°E, for example Inglefield Bay at about 75.5°N, 60°E. So 55°E at 75°N is probably in the sea.

Water

1378.text:
Latitude 75°N, longitude 57°E. This is in the Barents/Kara Sea region. Novaya Zemlya spans roughly 70.5°N to 77°N, with longitudes from 52°E to 69°E. At 75°N, Novaya Zemlya's western coast is around 56-58°E (the island is narrow and slants northeast). Southern island at 73°N: west coast about 54°E. At 75°N the west coast is around 58°E? Let me recall: Cape Zhelaniya is at 76.95°N, 68.55°E. Matochkin Strait is at about 73.3°N, from 56°E to 58°E. Moving northeast, the northern island's west coast near 75°N is about 59-60°E. Thus 57°E at 75°N is likely in the Barents Sea, west of the coast.

Water

1379.text:
Latitude 75°N, longitude 59°E. This lies in the Kara Sea region, east of Novaya Zemlya. Novaya Zemlya spans roughly 51°E to 69°E, running diagonally from southwest (around 70.5°N, 52°E) to northeast (76.9°N, 68°E). At 75°N, the island's west coast is around 56-58°E and the east coast is around 62-63°E. So 59°E at 75°N is probably on land.

More precisely, the west coast near 75°N is about 57°E (Mezhdusharsky area, Cape Zhelaniya at 77°N is 69°E). The northern island's coast at 75°N: the west coast is around 56°E, and the east coast near Russkaya Gavan at 76.2°N is 62.5°E. At 75°N the east coast is about 60°E (Krasino, Matochkin Shar is at 73.3°N). So 59°E is likely still land.

**Land**

1380.text:

At 75°N, the island's width: the southern island's northern part, around 75°N, the west coast is approximately 56-58°E and the east coast around 63°E to 68°E. At 75°N, the east coast is around 62°E. Specifically, Cape Zhelaniya at 76.9°N, 68.5°E. Krestovaya Guba around 73.5°N, 55°E. The Matochkin Strait is at 73.3°N, 56°E to 53°E. At 75°N, the west coast is about 59°E (Sulmeneva Bay region at 75.5°N is 58°E?). East coast at 75°N: Russkaya Gavan is at 76.2°N, 62.5°E; Tsivolki Bay at 75.5°N, ~62°E. Hmm, so at 75°N, 61°E is likely land, inside the island, which is covered by ice cap.

Land

1381.text:
Latitude 75°N, longitude 63°E lies in the Kara Sea region. Novaya Zemlya spans roughly 70°N–77°N and 51°E–69°E. At 75°N, Novaya Zemlya's northern island spans from about 55°E on the west coast to about 67°E at its east coast near 75°N? The island is narrow, about 100 km wide at places. At latitude 75°N, the west coast is around 56–58°E and the east coast around 63–65°E, since the island trends northeast. Cape Zhelaniya is at 76.95°N, 68.5°E. Matochkin Strait is at ~73.3°N, 56°E. At 75°N, the west coast is near 58°E (Mashigin Bay area?), and the east coast near 62°E? Cape Spory Navolok at 75.9°N, 60°E is on the west side... Actually, Severny Island's west coast near 76°N is at about 60°E, and the northern tip, Cape Zhelaniya at 68.5°E, means the coast runs northeast. At 75°N, the west coast is around 57–58°E and the east coast around 62–63°E (Russkaya Gavan is at 76.2°N, 62.6°E on the west... actually on the northwest coast). The east coast at 75°N: Cape Menshikov 75.7°N, 63°E? Hmm, Cape Menshikov is around 74.5°N? Uncertain. Given the island's width, 63°E at 75°N is likely near the east coast, probably land.

Land

1382.text:
Latitude 75°N, longitude 65°E is in the Kara Sea region. Novaya Zemlya spans roughly 70°E to 68°E at around 75°N, with its western coast near 56°E at 75°N. Its eastern coast lies around 68°E at 75°N, so 65°E falls inside Novaya Zemlya's northern island. Novaya Zemlya at 75°N runs from about 56°E to 68°E, so 65°E is land.

Checking further: the northern island at 75°N has a west coast around 57–58°E and an east coast around 68–69°E. Yes, 65°E is within it.

Land

1383.text:
Latitude 75°N, longitude 67°E. This is in the Kara Sea region. Novaya Zemlya spans roughly 70°-77°N, 51°-69°E. At 75°N, Novaya Zemlya's eastern coast is around 60-62°E at its northern island... So the point is water.

Water

1384.text:

If the longitude were west (69°W), it would be in northwest Greenland or the Baffin Bay area. At 75°N, 69°W, that is near Thule, Greenland (76.5°N, 68.7°W). Thule sits on the coast, and 75°N is slightly south of it, likely over the Greenland ice sheet or land, but the coordinates were given as positive, so east is the reading.

**Water**

1385.text:

1386.text:

Water

So 75.0°N, 85°E is likely just north of the coast, in the Kara Sea.

**Water**

Near 88°E, Cape Sterlegov at 75.4°N, so 75.0°N at 91°E is likely land, since the coast to the east is further north (Minin skerries is at 77°N, 90°E? No—Minin Skerries are around 75.5°N, 97°E). The coast at 91°E is about 76°N (Cape Sterlegov is on an island at 75.4°N 88.9°E; Taymyr mainland coast at Taymyr Bay ~75.9°N 90°E). So land.

Land

1396.text:

1415.text:

At 73°N the east coast is near 20-22°W (Jameson Land is at about 71°N). Further north, at 73°N, the coast around Kuhn Island and Hold with Hope sits near 21°W. So 31°W at 73°N is well inland, in the Greenland ice sheet or in the fjord region of Stauning Alps. The Stauning Alps are at about 72°N, 25°W, and Caledonian fjords like Kong Oscar Fjord are at 72°N, 24°W. So 31°W is further inland, on the ice sheet.

Land

1515.text:
Latitude 73.0°N, longitude -29.0° (29°W) falls in Greenland's northeast. Greenland's east coast around 73°N lies near Scoresby Sund, which is at about 70°N, 22°W. At 73°N the coast is around 20-22°W (Hold with Hope at 73.5°N, 20°W). So 29°W at 73°N is inland, within the ice sheet or the land of Greenland, which is at about 27°W near Kong Oscar Fjord (72°N, 24°W) and Kejser Franz Joseph Fjord (73°N, 25°W). Fjord inland extends to roughly 27°W at 73.5°N. At 29°W it's likely land, perhaps the area near Stauning Alps or ice cap.

Land

1516.text:
Latitude 73°N, longitude 27°W is in East Greenland, near Scoresby Sund. Scoresby Sund is at about 70°N, 22–27°W. At 73°N, 27°W, this is in the Greenland interior or the northeast coast area. The coast at 73°N lies around 20–22°W (Liverpool Land is at 70.5°N). Near 73°N, the coast is around Hold with Hope (73.5°N, 20°W), and Kong Oscar Fjord is at 72°N, 24–26°W. At 73°N, 27°W the position is inland, north of Kong Oscar Fjord, in Ymer Island/Geographical Society Island region, or the land west of there. That is land.

Land

1517.text:
Latitude 73°N, longitude 25°W is in East Greenland, near Scoresby Sund. Scoresby Sund lies around 70°N, 22°W. At 73°N, 25°W, the coast of Greenland... Traill Island is at about 72.5°N, 24°W, and Geographical Society Island is at 72.8°N, 22.8°W. Ymer Island is at about 73.1°N, 25°W. Ymer Ø spans roughly 72.9–73.3°N and 24–26°W. Kong Oscar Fjord lies to the south of it, and Kempe Fjord is around 72.3°N. Ymer Ø's center is about 73.0°N, 25.5°W, so this point is likely on land.

Land

1518.text:
Latitude 73.0°N, longitude 23.0°W is in East Greenland. Scoresby Sund lies at about 70°N, 22°W, and the coast at 73°N is near 20–22°W. Around 73°N, Greenland's coast runs roughly from Kap Brewster (70°N, 22°W) up to Kong Oscar Fjord (about 72°N, 24°W) and Kejser Franz Joseph Fjord (73°N, 24–27°W). Traveling north, Traill Ø is at 72.5°N, 24°W, and Ymer Ø is at 73°N, 24–25°W. At 73°N, 23°W the point is probably at the mouth of Kejser Franz Joseph Fjord, near Geographical Society Ø (72.7°N, 22.5–24°W). Geographical Society Ø spans roughly 71.8–72.8°N, so 73.0°N is slightly north of it. Hold With Hope is at about 73.5°N, 20–22°W. Kong Oscar Fjord's mouth is at about 72.3°N. At 73°N, the coast of Gauss Halvø/Ymer Ø is at the fjord's north side. The point at 23°W is most likely in the water of Kejser Franz Joseph Fjord's outer part or on Ymer Ø's east end. I'm not certain, but Ymer Ø's eastern tip is around 24°W, and the area just east of it, around 23°W, is the fjord's water, not land.

Water

1519.text:
Latitude 73.0°N, longitude 21.0°W is in northeast Greenland. Greenland's east coast around 73°N is near Scoresby Sund, which is at about 70°N, 22°W. At 73°N the coast sits near 21–22°W, around Kong Oscar Fjord and Traill Island. Kong Oscar Fjord is at about 72.5°N, 24°W. Traill Island is at about 72.5°N, 24°W, and Geographical Society Island is at about 72.8°N, 22.8°W. Hold With Hope is at about 73.5°N, 20°W. Clavering Island is at about 74.3°N, 20°W. So 73°N, 21°W is just east of Geographical Society Island and south of Hold With Hope. The Hold With Hope peninsula spans roughly 73–73.9°N and its southern tip is near 73.3°N, 20°W. The point at 73.0°N, 21°W would be in the sea, probably Greenland Sea near Fosters Bugt, which is the water between Hold with Hope and Gael Hamke Bugt. Gael Hamke Bugt is around 74°N, 21°W. Fosters Bugt is around 73.2°N, 21°W, so this is water.

Water

1520.text:
Latitude 73°N, longitude 19°W is in East Greenland, near Scoresby Sund area (Scoresby Sund is around 70°N, 22°W). At 73°N, 19°W is Greenland's coast: Kong Oscar Fjord is around 72°N, 24°W. Traill Island is at 72.5°N, 24°W. Further east is Ymer Island, Geographical Society Island (72.8°N, 22.5°W). At 19°W, 73°N: Hold with Hope peninsula is around 73.5°N, 20°W. The coast around Hold with Hope is at about 19-20°W, with Clavering Island at 74°N, 20°W. Coast at 73°N is near 20-21°W (Kap Broer Ruys is at 73.5°N, 20.5°W). So 19°W is east of the coast, so water.

**Water**

1536.text:

1537.text:

1549.text:

1551.text:
Latitude 73°N, longitude 43°E is in the Barents Sea, east of Novaya Zemlya's southern part? Novaya Zemlya spans roughly 51°E to 69°E, so 43°E is well west of it. The Russian mainland coast is at about 68°N at that longitude, and Kolguev Island is at 69°N, 49°E. So 73°N, 43°E is open sea.

1552.text:
Latitude 73°N, longitude 45°E. That is in the Barents Sea, east of Svalbard and north of Novaya Zemlya's southern part. Novaya Zemlya spans roughly 51°E to 69°E, with its western coast around 52–55°E at 73°N. So 45°E is west of it, in open sea. The Russian mainland is at about 68°N, so it's far south.

Water

1553.text:
Latitude 73°N, longitude 47°E. That is in the Barents Sea / Kara Sea region. Novaya Zemlya spans roughly 70.5–77°N, 51–69°E. At 47°E, 73°N, it is west of Novaya Zemlya's southern island, which starts around 51°E. So it is in the Barents Sea.

Water

1554.text:
Latitude 73°N, longitude 49°E is in the Barents Sea, east of Novaya Zemlya's western coast? Novaya Zemlya spans roughly 51°E to 69°E, and at 73°N its southwestern part is near 54°E. At 49°E, 73°N, that is west of Novaya Zemlya, in the Barents Sea.

Water

1555.text:
Latitude 73°N, longitude 51°E is in the Barents Sea, near the southern tip of Novaya Zemlya. Novaya Zemlya's southern island begins around 70.5°N, with the Kara Strait at about 70.5°N, 58°E. At longitude 51°E and 73°N, the western coast of Novaya Zemlya sits at roughly 52-55°E for the latitudes around 73°N. For instance, Cape Zhelaniya is at 77°N, 69°E, but the west coast near Matochkin Shar (73.3°N) is at about 55°E. So 51°E at 73°N is west of the coast and therefore in the sea.

Water

1556.text:
Latitude 73°N, longitude 53°E is in the Barents Sea/Kara Sea region. Novaya Zemlya's southern island spans roughly 70.5°N–76°N, and its longitude is about 52°E–68°E. At 73°N, the west coast of Novaya Zemlya sits around 54°E, so 53°E is probably just west of the coast, in the Barents Sea.

Checking in more detail: Cape Zhelaniya is at 76.9°N, 68.5°E. Near Matochkin Shar (73.3°N), the west coast is around 53.5°E, and the strait runs from about 52.5°E at the west entrance. So 73.0, 53.0 is just west of the coast, in the water.

Water

1557.text:
Latitude 73°N, longitude 55°E. That's in the Barents Sea/Kara Sea area. Novaya Zemlya spans roughly 70.5–77°N and 51–69°E. At 73°N, the southern island of Novaya Zemlya's west coast lies around 53–55°E. Novaya Zemlya's west coast at 73°N: Southern island near Matochkin Strait (73.3°N) – the strait lies at about 73.3°N, 55–56°E. The west coast at that latitude is about 54°E. So 55°E at 73°N is likely land, just east of the west coast, on the island's western part.

Matochkin Strait runs from about 73.4°N, 53.5°E (west mouth) to 73.3°N, 58°E (east). At 73.0°N, just south of the strait, so land.

Land

1558.text:
Latitude 73°N, longitude 57°E is in the Barents Sea/Kara Sea region. Novaya Zemlya spans roughly 70.5°N–77°N, with longitudes from about 51°E to 69°E. At 73°N, the southern island of Novaya Zemlya runs from around 53°E on the west coast to about 57°E on the east side. Near 73°N the island is narrow, with the west coast at about 54°E and the east coast near 57°E, so the point is uncertain.

Checking details: Matochkin Strait is at about 73.3°N, separating the two islands, and it runs from about 53°E to 56.5°E. At 73.0°N, just south of the strait, the island is the southern one. The east coast there, on the Kara Sea side, is around 56–57°E. The coast near Cape Dmitry... Belushya Guba is at 71.5°N, 52°E. On the Kara side at 73°N, the coast is approximately 55.5°E. This would put 57°E in the Kara Sea water.

Water

1559.text:
Latitude 73°N, longitude 59°E. This is in the Kara Sea region, east of Novaya Zemlya. Novaya Zemlya spans roughly 51°E to 69°E, with the southern island's northern part around 73-76°N. At 73°N, the island's east coast is around 56-58°E, for Severny Island (north island), which begins around 73.5°N at Matochkin Strait (~73.3°N). The southern island's northern coast at Matochkin Strait is about 73.3°N, with the southern island's east coast at 73°N near 57°E... The Kara Sea coast around 72°N is at ~55°E (Cape Zhelaniya is at 76.9°N, 68.5°E). Near Matochkin Strait the east end is at about 56°E. South of that, the east coast trends southwest: at 71°N it's around 54°E. So at 73°N the east coast is about 56°E, and 59°E would be in the Kara Sea.

Water

1560.text:
Latitude 73°N, longitude 61°E. That's in the Kara Sea region... Novaya Zemlya spans roughly 70.5–77°N, and longitudes 51–69°E. At latitude 73, Novaya Zemlya's southern island lies around 55–58°E at 71-73°N; the island's east coast at 73°N is about 57°E. The Kara Sea is east of that, so 61°E at 73°N is in the Kara Sea.

Water

1561.text:
Latitude 73°N, longitude 63°E lies in the Kara Sea, to the east of Novaya Zemlya. Novaya Zemlya's southern island reaches about 60°E at around 70-71°N, and its northern island extends to roughly 69°E at 76°N. At 73°N, the island's east coast sits near 55°E on the west side, and the Kara Sea coast near 58°E. So 63°E at 73°N is east of the island, in the Kara Sea.

Water

1562.text:
Latitude 73°N, longitude 65°E. That's in the Kara Sea, east of Novaya Zemlya (which spans roughly 51°E to 69°E at its northern extent). At 73°N, Novaya Zemlya's southern island sits around 70-77°N, and its eastern coast at that latitude is about 56-58°E. So 65°E at 73°N is east of the island, in the Kara Sea. Yamal Peninsula reaches about 73°N at its northern tip near 70°E, and at 73°N the Yamal's west coast is around 67-69°E. So 65°E is in the water.

Water

1563.text:
Latitude 73°N, longitude 67°E. That's in the Kara Sea region, east of Novaya Zemlya (which spans roughly 51–69°E at those latitudes). Novaya Zemlya's southern island sits at about 70–73°N, with its western coast near 52–55°E and its eastern coast near 58–60°E at 73°N. So 67°E is east of the island, in the Kara Sea. The Yamal Peninsula reaches about 73°N at roughly 70–72°E, and at 67°E the peninsula's western coast is around 66–68°E at 70°N, but at 73°N it's the Kara Sea (the peninsula's tip is around 73°N, 69–70°E). Therefore 67°E, 73°N is water.

Water

1564.text:
Latitude 73°N, longitude 69°E. This is in the Kara Sea region? The Yamal Peninsula extends to about 73°N at 70°E. The Yamal's northern tip is around 73°N, 68-70°E. Yamal peninsula spans roughly 66.5°N to 73°N, longitudes 66°E to 72°E. At 73°N, the northern tip of Yamal is near Cape Skuratova at 73.0°N, 69°E roughly. Belyy Island is at 73°N, 70°E. Cape Skuratov is around 73.1°N, 69.8°E? Hmm. The west coast of the northern Yamal at 73°N is about 68.5°E, and the coast runs northeast. Point 69°E at 73°N is likely land, near the coast.

Land

1565.text:
Latitude 73°N, longitude 71°E. That is in the Kara Sea, east of Novaya Zemlya (which lies at about 55–68°E). At 73°N, 71°E, the Yamal Peninsula is at about 66–72°E, but its northern tip is around 73°N at 70-72°E. Yamal's northern end reaches about 73°N near Cape Kharasavey at 71.1°E, 71.2°N... Actually Kharasavey is at about 71.2°N. The peninsula's northernmost point is around 73°N at roughly 69–70°E (Cape Mare-Sale is at 69.7°N). Yamal extends north to about 73.0°N at Bely Island (73.3°N, 70°E), which is an island in the Kara Sea. Yamal's mainland tip is about 71.5°N. So 73°N, 71°E is likely just south of Bely Island, in water.

Water

1566.text:
Latitude 73°N, longitude 73°E. That's in the Kara Sea region... Let's check: the Yamal Peninsula extends to about 73°N at longitude ~70-72°E. Yamal Peninsula's northern tip is around 73°N, 69-70°E. At 73°E, 73°N, this is in the Gulf of Ob/Kara Sea area. The Ob Gulf lies around 72-73°E, extending south from ~73°N. The Gydan Peninsula is to the east of the Ob Gulf, at ~75-80°E. The Gulf of Ob is narrow at roughly 72-75°E in the north. At 73°N, the Ob Gulf spans about 72–74°E? Then the Gydan side (Gydan Bay is to the east, the Taz Gulf at 75-78°E). The northern Gulf of Ob at 73°N: the Yamal east coast is around 72.5°E at 72°N, and the Gydan west coast ~74°E. So 73°E at 73°N is likely water.

**Water**

1567.text:
Latitude 73°N, longitude 75°E lies in the Kara Sea, north of the Yamal Peninsula and the Gydan Peninsula. The Yamal Peninsula reaches about 73°N at its northern tip near 70°E. At 75°E, 73°N, the point is east of Yamal and lies in the Kara Sea, which includes the Ob Gulf area farther south. The Gydan Peninsula's northern coast is around 73°N at 80°E, and its coast near 75°E is about 72°N. The point is therefore probably water.

Water

1568.text:
Latitude 73°N, longitude 77°E: this is in the Kara Sea region. The Taymyr Peninsula lies further east (~100°E), and the Yamal Peninsula reaches about 73°N at roughly 70-72°E. Gydan Peninsula spans ~75-82°E, with its northern tip around 73-74°N. The Gulf of Ob lies to the west of Gydan at ~73°E, and the Taz/Yenisei gulf to the east at ~80°E. At 77°E, 73°N the point is in the northern Gydan Peninsula, which extends north to about 73.5°N near the Neupokoeva Island area. So it is likely land.

Land

1569.text:
Latitude 73°N, longitude 79°E is in northern Russia, near the Kara Sea coast. The Gydan Peninsula reaches about 73°N, and the Yamal Peninsula lies around 70°E. At 79°E, the coast sits near 72-73°N at the Gulf of Yenisei/Taymyr area. The Yenisei Gulf is around 80°E, with the Gydan Peninsula to the west at roughly 77-78°E. The Gydan Peninsula's northern tip is about 73.5°N at 79°E. The Ob Gulf is at about 73°E, and the Gydan Peninsula spans from the Ob to the Yenisei gulfs, so 79°E at 73°N is probably land. The Yenisei Gulf's western shore is around 79-80°E at 72°N, and Gydan Bay is at about 74°N. It's more likely land.

Land

1570.text:
Latitude 73°N, longitude 81°E lies in the Kara Sea region. The Taymyr Peninsula reaches about 77°N at 100°E, but at 81°E the coast is lower. The Gulf of Ob and Yenisei Gulf are near 72-73°N. The Yamal Peninsula is at 66-73°N, 66-72°E. The Gydan Peninsula lies around 70-72°N, 76-80°E. At 81°E, 73°N, the area is the Kara Sea. Between the Yenisei mouth (~82°E at 72°N) and the Gydan coast, the Yenisei Gulf runs north to about 73°N, so the point is likely in the Yenisei Gulf or just off it, which is water. Islands such as Sibiryakov Island (~72.8°N, 79°E) are nearby. The point at 81°E is east of Sibiryakov, in the gulf mouth, which is water.

Water

1571.text:
Latitude 73°N, longitude 83°E lies in the Kara Sea region. The Taymyr Peninsula reaches about 77°N at 100°E. At 83°E, the coast near the Gulf of Yenisei and Ob lies around 73°N. The Yenisei Gulf is around 80-82°E at 72-73°N, and the Gydan Peninsula is east of the Ob Gulf. The Ob Gulf is around 73°E. Yenisei Gulf is about 80°E at 72°N. Land at 83°E, 73°N... the east shore of the Yenisei Gulf is at about 83°E at 72-73°N (Ust-Port is at 84°E, 69.7°N). The Yenisei Gulf extends north to about 73°N at roughly 80°E. 1609.text:

So 73°N is about 200 miles offshore, and the answer is water.

Water

1619.text:

1620.text:

1627.text:

1630.text:
Latitude 71.0°N, longitude -159.0° is in northern Alaska. Utqiaġvik (Barrow) sits at about 71.29°N, 156.79°W. At -159.0 longitude, the coast near Peard Bay and Wainwright is around 70.6°N, 160°W. At longitude -159, the coast lies at roughly 70.9°N, since the coast runs southwest to northeast between Wainwright (70.64, -160.0) and Barrow (71.29, -156.8). Interpolating at -159: about 70.64 + (1/3.2)*0.65 ≈ 70.84°N. So 71.0 is slightly north of the coast, which would be water. The coastline is bumpy, though. Near Peard Bay, the Seagull Islands and Point Franklin (70.9°N, -158.8) project north. Point Franklin is at about 70.93°N, 158.8°W, a spit extending northeast. At 71.0 it would still be north of that, so water.

Water

1631.text:
Latitude 71.0°N, longitude -157.0° is near Utqiagvik (Barrow), Alaska, which sits at about 71.29°N, -156.79°W. At 71.0°N, the point is about 20 miles south of Barrow, which is inland tundra, so it is land.

1632.text:
Latitude 71.0°N, longitude -155.0° is near Utqiagvik (Barrow), Alaska, which sits at about 71.29°N, -156.79°W. At -155.0°, 71.0°N, we are east-southeast of Barrow. The coast east of Barrow runs southeast toward Dease Inlet (about 71.0°N, -155.5°W) and Admiralty Bay (-154.5°W), and Smith Bay's mouth is around 70.0°N... Actually, Dease Inlet lies at approximately 71.0°N, -155.3°W, so this point is likely in the water of Dease Inlet.

Dease Inlet extends from about 71.1°N at its mouth down to about 70.9°N, roughly between -155.5° and -155.0°. The point seems to be within or at the edge of the inlet, so it's likely water.

Water

1633.text:

Water

1645.text:

Water

1646.text:

At 127°W and 71°N, the area is Banks Island, whose southeastern part reaches about 72°N and whose southern coast is near 71.0°N at 125°W. Cape Kellett is at 71.98°N, 125.9°W, and Banks Island's southwest corner is at about 71.9°N, 125.9°W... so I need to place the coast more carefully.

Banks Island spans roughly 71.0–74.5°N, and its southern tip, Cape Kellett, is around 71.98°N. Its west coast runs north from there, at about 125.5°W to 124°W. The island's southwestern coast is therefore near 72°N, so 71°N at 127°W lies south of the island, in Amundsen Gulf.

Mainland Canada's Parry Peninsula is at about 70°N, so 71°N is north of it, which also points to water.

**Water**

1647.text:
Latitude 71.0°N, longitude -125.0° is in northern Canada. Banks Island's southern part lies around 71–72°N, 119–125°W. Amundsen Gulf is between Banks Island and the mainland, at roughly 70–71°N, 120–126°W. Banks Island's southwestern tip, Cape Kellett, is at about 71.98°N, 125.9°W. At 71.0°N, 125°W, the west coast of Banks Island is around 124.5–125°W near Sachs Harbour (71.98°N, 125.2°W). Sachs Harbour is at 72°N. So at 71.0°N, the point is south of Banks Island, in Amundsen Gulf.

The mainland coast is at about 69.5°N, and Amundsen Gulf is between them, so 71.0°N is water.

**Water**

1648.text:

Water

1649.text:
Latitude 71.0°N, longitude -121.0° (121°W) is in northern Canada. Banks Island spans roughly 71–74.5°N and 115–125°W. Victoria Island lies further east, at about 105–118°W. The mainland coast near Amundsen Gulf is at about 69–70°N.

The southern coast of Banks Island runs around 71.2°N at 121–123°W, and the island's southeast part is near Sachs Harbour (71.98°N, 125.2°W). So 71.0°N, 121°W would be south of Banks Island's southern coast, in Prince of Wales Strait or Amundsen Gulf. Prince of Wales Strait lies between Banks and Victoria Islands, at about 72–73°N and 118°W. At 71°N, 121°W, the area is Amundsen Gulf's eastern part, near Cape Parry's longitude of 124°W at 70.2°N. Victoria Island's western coast, near Wollaston Peninsula, is around 70–71°N and 117°W. So 121°W is water.

**Water**

1650.text:
Latitude 71.0°N, longitude -119.0° is in northern Canada. Victoria Island spans roughly 69–73.5°N and 100–118°W. At -119 and 71, that would be just west of Victoria Island's western edge, in Prince of Wales Strait or Amundsen Gulf. Banks Island's eastern coast is about -120°, and Prince of Wales Strait lies between Banks Island and Victoria Island at roughly -117 to -119°. Banks Island's east coast at 71°N is around -119.5°, near Sachs Harbour (71.98N, -125), which is farther west. Banks Island's southeastern part extends to about -119 at 72°N. At 71°N the east coast is near -120.5 or so, and the strait is around -118 to -119. Victoria Island's west coast at 71°N is around -117.5 (Prince Albert Peninsula extends to -116 to -118 at 71–73°N). So -119 is likely in the strait.

Water

1651.text:
Latitude 71.0°N, longitude -117.0°W lies in northern Canada. Victoria Island spans roughly 69–73.7°N and 100–119°W. At 71°N, 117°W, that is the western part of Victoria Island, near Prince Albert Sound and Minto Inlet. Minto Inlet runs from about 71.5°N, 117.5°W southward to about 71°N, 117°W, so the point could fall in the inlet. Prince Albert Sound lies further south, at roughly 70°N, 115–117°W.

Minto Inlet's mouth is at Prince of Wales Strait around 72°N, 118°W, and the inlet extends southeast to about 71.0°N, 117°W. Its head is near Holman (Ulukhaktok), which is at 70.7°N, 117.8°W. Holman sits on the west coast of Victoria Island, south of Minto Inlet. Minto Inlet's head is at around 71.3°N, 116.5°W. So 71.0°N, 117.0°W is probably within the inlet's southern part, though it is uncertain.

Minto Inlet is about 20–30 km wide, running NNE to SSW, with its head near 71.4°N, 117°W, so the point is probably in the water.

**Water**

1652.text:

At 71°N, 115°W, this is in the western part of Victoria Island, near Prince Albert Sound's northern region. Prince Albert Sound is at about 70°N, 116°W, and it cuts into the island from the west. Minto Inlet is at about 71.5°N, 117°W. At 115°W and 71°N, this is likely inland on the island, east of Minto Inlet and north of Prince Albert Sound. Land.

Land

1653.text:
Latitude 71.0°N, longitude -113.0°W is in the Canadian Arctic. Victoria Island spans roughly 69°-73.5°N and 101°-119°W. At 71°N, 113°W, the location falls in the interior of Victoria Island's northwest part. Victoria Island's west coast at 71°N is around 118°W (Prince Albert Sound is around 70°N, 115°W). At 71°N, north of the sound, it is likely land (the Wollaston Peninsula is to the south, and the area north of the sound is Victoria Island's main body). So it is land.

Land

1654.text:
Latitude 71.0°N, longitude -111.0° is in northern Canada. Victoria Island spans roughly 69°–73.5°N and 100°–119°W. At 71°N, 111°W, that falls in the interior of Victoria Island. Victoria Island's northern part near Prince Albert Sound is around 70-71°N, 115°W. Wollaston Peninsula and Storkerson Peninsula are around 70-71°N and 111-115°W. Storkerson Bay is around 72°N, 125°W, so that's not close. Hmm, Richard Collinson Inlet is at about 71.5°N, 117°W. Prince Albert Sound is at 70°N, 115°W. Near 111°W at 71°N, Victoria Island's east coast is along Dease Strait, at about 69°N, and Victoria Strait near 69.5°N, 101°W. The east coast of the island's north part runs along Viscount Melville Sound... Actually, Victoria Island's northeast area (Prince Albert Peninsula is at the west). The northeast area near 71°N, 111°W is part of Victoria Island's interior, such as Goldsmith Channel near 70.5°N, 100°W. So it is land.

Land

1655.text:
Latitude 71.0°N, longitude -109.0° is in the Canadian Arctic. Victoria Island spans roughly 69°–73.5°N and 101°–119°W. At longitude -109, the island's southern coast is around 68.5–69°N (Cambridge Bay is at 69.1°N, 105°W). Northward at -109, we'd be at Prince Albert Sound's area... At 109°W, the north coast of Victoria Island is at Richard Collinson Inlet around 71–72°N, and Hadley Bay lies near 72°N, 108°W. **Land**

1656.text:
Latitude 71.0°N, longitude -107.0°W lies in the Canadian Arctic. Victoria Island spans roughly 69°–73.5°N and 100°–119°W. At longitude -107, Victoria Island's southern coast sits around 69°N, near Cambridge Bay at 69.1°N, -105°W. At 71°N, -107°W, this falls in the interior of Victoria Island's eastern part. Victoria Island's northeast coast near Prince Albert Sound... the island's eastern edge at 71°N is around -104°W to -105°W (Hadley Bay is at around 72.5°N, -108°W). So 71°N, -107°W is likely land, in the Storkerson Peninsula area.

Land

1657.text:
